title: Special Topics in Bioengineering; Model-Based Public Policy
description:
Equivalent of differential equations, experience in coding is preferable.

The first part of the class will be dedicated to learning what public policy is, a few case studies will be reviewed. In particular, we will analyze cases where the use of models can be contrasted with public policy without models. The use of different models used in public policy will be discussed. The course will focus on learning agent based modeling (ABM), which has been used in many areas of science, including social and health sciences. Specific examples will be presented and students will create a model for a specific policy need.
